summary.headline: SBI Life FY26 VoNB rose 12% to INR66.7bn at a 27.5% margin, but PAT grew only 2% to INR24.7bn due to GST and Labour Code one-offs.
summary.overview: FY26 new business premium grew 20% to INR425.5bn with a 21.4% private market share, and individual APE grew 13% to INR221.1bn. Reported PAT rose only 2% to INR24.7bn; excluding GST and Labour Code impacts it would have been INR31.2bn (up 29%). VoNB was INR66.7bn (27.5% margin), and excluding GST it would have been INR70.3bn at a 29% margin. Management guided to around 14% growth and a 26-28% VoNB margin range, with the GST impact on commissions and expenses now reflected for the second half of FY26.

financial_highlights.change: +2% YoY; ex-GST and Labour Code INR31.2bn, +29%

segments.name: Individual protection
segments.commentary: Individual protection APE INR10.3bn (+24%); pure protection APE grew 122%; protection overall 9% of APE at INR22.4bn (+10%).

segments.name: Participating (par)
segments.commentary: Individual par APE INR17.3bn, up 133% on a low base after new par launches; par sum assured up 166%.

segments.name: Non-par guaranteed savings
segments.commentary: INR42.7bn of business, 19% of individual APE; a new non-par product was launched in January to reflect current yields.

segments.name: ULIP
segments.commentary: INR144.2bn, 65% of individual APE versus 70% last year; management cites a 66:34 ULIP:non-ULIP mix on an individual regular-premium basis.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group new business premium INR127.7bn (30% of new business premium, +39%); group credit life APE INR2.9bn (+14%).

segments.name: Bancassurance (SBI and RRBs)
segments.commentary: 60% of total APE; individual APE INR141.2bn (+11%); SBI branch productivity INR6.0m (+10%).

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Individual APE INR68.6bn (+15%); agent productivity INR2.6 lakh; non-ULIP share rose from 34% to 39%; over 1.2 lakh agents added gross and 120 branches opened.

segments.name: Other channels (direct, brokers, online, aggregators)
segments.commentary: Grew 22% and contributed 11% of total APE; online channel grew 47% on APE (own website 48-50%).

guidance_outlook: Medium-term APE growth target of around 14%, in line with the 3-5 year CAGR; FY26 individual APE growth was 13% versus 13% guidance.
VoNB margin guided to 26-28% range for FY27-28, with the company aiming to report above 27%; management declined to extend the range to FY27-29.
GST impact on first-year commission for business written before 22 September 2025 is about 1.8-1.9% of margin on an annual basis; management says it is largely absorbed in the 27.5% margin.
Opex ratio expected to carry a full year of GST in FY27, but management expects it not to rise materially; IT and branch spend to continue.
Deferred annuity (regular-pay) product targeted for launch by June 2026, otherwise the next quarter.
Ind AS transition: forbearance sought, with adoption from 1 April 2027.
capex_capacity: Opened 120 new branches in FY26 and added over 1.2 lakh agents on a gross basis; management says newer branches are on track but not yet at breakeven.
Continued investment planned in branches, IT infrastructure and agency training; management says no other major expense is planned beyond IT strengthening.
Solvency of 1.90 funded by internal accruals with no fresh capital raised; the company is assessing Ind AS and RBC impacts.
demand_pricing: Customers are investing where they see value despite geopolitical volatility; February and March growth was described as decent, and management expects continued sales growth.
Q4 bancassurance sales declined year on year; management said the whole insurance sector was sluggish in Q4 and that banca met its internal budget for the year.
Non-par pricing is being adjusted with interest rates; a new non-par product replaced the existing one to reflect current yields, passing some benefit to customers.
Management is not planning higher sum assured ULIPs for now, but will decide on launching them in due course.
Online business grew 47% on APE; 99.7% of individual proposals were submitted digitally and 57% of individual policies went through automated underwriting.

qa_highlights.question: Is the persistency assumption change a negative in the VNB walk, and is there a reset in persistency assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is about 50 bps and not significant; changes were minor refinements across mortality, persistency and expenses, with a persistency improvement from long-term protection.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 14% growth at risk given banca grew only 9-11% for three years, and is banca realistically 10-11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not guide channel-level growth; growth would come from agency and other channels, with 14% as an optimal mix. Protection growth is ticket-size-light and supports policy count.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 27-28% margin guidance conservative given FY26 ex-GST margin of 29%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a matter of perception; the range gives flexibility to balance 14% growth with margin, and the product mix is being improved.

qa_highlights.question: What is the GST impact on margins going forward and the opex ratio trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: GST for the second half is already in the 27.5% margin, and the full-year effect is about 1.8-1.9%. Opex ratio would be about 5.5% without GST and the Labour Code versus 5.3% in FY25; the 6.1% reflects GST and Labour Code costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EV operating variance strongly positive while VNB assumptions were strengthened?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said positive variance comes mainly from mortality and persistency, with lower expenses contributing. Assumption changes are minor refinements, and new and in-force business differ in product mix. Economic variance of 3.66% is split as 2.15% from equity, with the balance from bonds.

qa_highlights.question: Does open architecture in banca pose a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is unaware of any such decision, that RBI guidelines are draft and due from 1 July and do not mention open architecture, and that the company will respond to regulatory changes if they arise.

risks_watch: GST treatment on commissions: the full-year impact in FY27 and whether it is offset by product mix.
Persistency: the 61st-month drop linked to COVID-era ULIP sales, and the effect of assumption refinements on VNB.
Banca growth at around 9-11%: the agency and other channels must carry the 14% target.
Equity market volatility affecting ULIP demand and the 65% ULIP share of individual APE.
Regulatory: draft RBI guidelines effective 1 July, Ind AS transition from FY28 and RBC framework, plus any open architecture mandate for banks.
Deferred annuity launch timing (June 2026 target) and non-par repricing with yield volatility.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margin and solvency, and firm on guidance; management repeatedly declined to give channel-level margin, Credit Life, and protection-split figures, and deferred several questions to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: Excluding GST impact, VoNB would have been INR70.3 billion, representing 18% growth with a VoNB margin of 29%, an improvement of 150 basis points.
So we stuck to our range and we will continue to maintain that kind of margin in coming years also.
So our endeavor is to launch this deferred annuity product in this quarter itself.

growth.why: Management guides medium-term APE growth of around 14% (in line with 3-5 year CAGR of 12.9% for individual APE), backed by 120 new branches, 1.2 lakh gross agent additions, a deferred annuity launch targeted by June 2026, and a new non-par product, but no concrete order or capacity numbers tie the 14% to specific delivery.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: VoNB margin guided to 26-28% for FY27-28 with aim to report above 27%, against 27.5% in FY26 and 29% ex-GST, but full-year GST drag of about 1.8-1.9% and opex ratio at 6.1% vs 5.3% in FY25 cap any expansion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 120 branches opened in FY26 and over 1.2 lakh gross agents added, with newer branches not yet at breakeven, so further branch and agency build-out is ongoing, though no branch count target was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides around 14% APE growth (FY26 individual APE +13%, 3-5 year CAGR 12.9%), with Feb-Mar growth described as decent, but Q4 banca sales fell YoY and banca is only growing 9-11%, so agency and other channels must carry the target.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Solvency of 1.90 vs 1.50 requirement funded by internal accruals with no fresh capital raised, and management says no other major expense is planned beyond IT strengthening; utilisation is not a relevant metric for an insurer.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held guidance at around 14% APE growth and 26-28% VoNB margin and declined to extend the margin range to FY27-29, leaving no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Full-year GST impact of about 1.8-1.9% of margin, a full year of GST in opex, and banca growth of only 9-11% for three years put the 14% growth and 26-28% margin under pressure if agency growth lags.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Deferred annuity (regular-pay) product targeted to go live by June 2026, otherwise next quarter, and a new non-par product was already launched in January 2026 to reflect current yields.

rows.label: Draft RBI open-architecture guidelines effective 1 July
rows.why: RBI draft guidelines are due from 1 July; management says they do not mention open architecture, but banca is 60% of APE and any mandate would hit the core channel.

rows.label: Ind AS transition with adoption from 1 April 2027
rows.why: Management sought forbearance and is assessing Ind AS and RBC impacts, so reported earnings metrics could shift from FY28 once adopted.

rows.label: Group new business growth
rows.why: Group new business premium rose 39% to INR127.7bn (30% of new business premium), offering a second growth engine that partly offsets slower banca.
